title: Eleven Built Pairings
lede: Eleven pairings, each one actually built — ladder, stat spread, race, background, gear and gate audit — rather than estimated from a roster. Every card carries the numbers from its own sheet and links out to it.
cards_note: The same carry is a different build on every card. Bombard's Act III AoE runs 2–3 and its Endurance 4–5 across five sheets, because the feats, race and ladder differ by partner. That spread has not been averaged away.

cards.title: Per pair, not per chassis
cards.body: Nothing here is a shared roster score. Each pairing was built as a pair, so the halves are tuned to each other.

cards.title: Two numbers, counted once
cards.body: Coverage is the seven non-damage axes, 105 across the run. Damage coverage is delivered damage with the reach discount applied. The nine-axis total is not used: across a field it correlates with delivered damage at 0.00.

cards.title: Reach is a discount
cards.body: Applied to the single-target term only — ranged 1.00, hybrid 0.95, mobile 0.95/1.00, static 0.85/0.90. A pair with no ranged or hybrid half takes a further 0.9 on crowd.

cards.title: The flag
cards.body: A body under 3.0 in a fight type worth 40% or more of that act has nothing useful to do there. 5 + 0 is worse than 3 + 3, and this is where the tables say so.

footer: Scores read from each sheet's own radar · load-bearing mod claims read from the installed .pak archives · 18 August 2026

splits.a: Warlock 17 (The Fiend) / Sorcerer 3 (Draconic) · Astral Half-Elf · Charlatan
splits.b: Cleric 17 (Zeal / Hazoret) / Bard 3 (Lore) · Shadar-kai · Folk Hero

ember-fervor.tagline: A blast carry whose area mode is the same beams retargeted, beside a heavy-armour Cleric who pays for the fights the beams cannot end. One decision shapes both halves: neither character's damage runs on a rest clock, so the 120-supply long rest is chosen, never forced.
ember-fervor.shape: The pair covers damage, endurance and durability outright; it is thin on Control from Act III and it has exactly one healer
ember-fervor.damage: This pair owns the crowd fight from Act II onward and merely keeps pace in the boss fight — the priority column never doubles the way the crowd column does

splits.a: Wizard 6 / Blood Hunter 14 · Evocation + Order of the Profane Soul · Astral Half-Elf · Urchin
splits.b: Cleric 17 / Bard 3 · Zeal (Hazoret) + College of Lore · Lizardfolk · Soldier

bombard-fervor.tagline: Two fire casters who never compete for a concentration slot: Bombard brands one creature into blanket save-Disadvantage at no concentration cost, and Sculpt Spells lets him drop Fireball on a partner standing in melee. The single decision that shapes both halves is that the support, not the carry, owns the deep slot table.
bombard-fervor.shape: Five additive axes saturate by Act I — the shape to read is Sustain single-sourced, Saves thin early, and a carry whose area damage is capped at 3rd-level slots for the whole run
bombard-fervor.damage: This pair owns crowds in every act and merely keeps pace with bosses — and the crowd half is carried by the character labelled "support"

splits.b: Cleric 17 / Bard 3 · Zeal (Hazoret) · College of Lore · Astral Half-Elf · Sage

volley-fervor.tagline: The purest mode-switch AoE in the list beside the anchor that keeps it standing. Volley points the same at-will attack routine at a crowd — no save, no slot, no concentration — and pays for it with a save package that only Lone Wolf's second +4 repairs.
volley-fervor.shape: Two damage axes covered from character 12 onward, one healer, and a control hole neither half fills
volley-fervor.damage: The pair owns crowds from character 12 and only ever survives Act I's

hexplate-fervor.tagline: Two heavy-armour Charisma-and-Wisdom bodies that fight from the front and never run dry. The decision that shapes both halves is order: Hexplate spends ten levels as a Warlock in plate before it is allowed to be a Paladin, and Fervor covers every crowd on its own until the Eldritch Cone arrives at character 10.
hexplate-fervor.shape: Two durable, endless bodies with a real control hole in Act I and no Dexterity save anywhere
hexplate-fervor.damage: This pair owns crowds from character 10 onward and merely keeps pace on priority targets all run

splits.a: Cleric 3 (Twilight) / Monk 17 · Way of the Ascendant Dragon · Astral Elf · Urchin
splits.b: Cleric 17 (Zeal, Hazoret) / Bard 3 · College of Lore · Half-Orc · Folk Hero

breath-fervor.tagline: Breath of the Dragon replaces one attack, so the Monk's area mode costs no bonus action, no concentration and no second resource — and Wisdom being the Monk's primary stat in Listo makes the Cleric dip free in points. The pair is built around that one fact, and pays for it by having no ranged body at all.
breath-fervor.shape: A pair that is never short of damage, never short of a healer, and has no answer at all to a body it cannot walk to
breath-fervor.damage: The pair owns crowd fights in every act and puts a passenger on the field in every boss fight

splits.a: Cleric 17 / Fighter 3 · War Domain · Battle Master · Wood Elf · Outlander
splits.b: Sorcerer 17 / Cleric 1 / Fighter 2 · Storm Sorcery · Tempest dip · Shadar-kai · Charlatan

crozier-riptide.tagline: A weapon Cleric whose slots are never the pair's damage, beside a Sorcerer whose one Metamagic pick covers 100% of the party. Twinned Haste is the thesis — Crozier turns the extra action into two more swings, Riptide into a second levelled cast — and because Riptide fights from range, this is the one Cleric pairing that is not melee-locked.
crozier-riptide.shape: A carry that never runs out of resources beside a support that never runs out of actions — the hole is Endurance, and it is Riptide's number
crozier-riptide.damage: The pair owns crowds outright and merely keeps pace on priority targets — and the weighted figure falls from Act II to Act III because the fight mix moves toward the half it is weaker at

splits.b: Fighter 1 / Wizard 19 · School of Necromancy · Fey Eladrin · Sage

crozier-charnel.tagline: A Cleric that fights with a weapon so its slots stay free, beside a Necromancer whose slots buy bodies. One decision shapes both halves: Animate Dead++ removes the undead cap entirely, so the pair answers the duo's action-economy problem with four to eight extra bodies instead of with spells — and Crozier is built so none of those spells were needed for damage anyway.
crozier-charnel.shape: The only axis with a genuine hole is Sustain, and it is a threshold axis that Crozier already covers alone — every other axis has two sources
crozier-charnel.damage: This pair owns crowds in every act and closes the gap on priority targets only in Act III — which is the act where the fight mix stops rewarding crowds

bombard-chains.tagline: Two control engines on the short-rest clock, and only one concentration bar between them. Bombard's Brand of the Sapping Scar costs no concentration at all; Chains of Carceri is a free Hold Monster that leaves the pact slots untouched — so the debuff and the lock never compete for the same resource.
bombard-chains.shape: A control pair that pays for it in single-target damage and in bodies on the field
bombard-chains.damage: This pair owns crowds from character 5 and merely keeps up with bosses all run — the boss answer is the Brand, not the damage

bombard-riptide.tagline: Two ranged casters, both throwing area, with Twinned Haste handing each of them a third action. Every additive axis saturates by Act II — and nobody can heal anybody, which is the one decision the whole sheet is built around.
bombard-riptide.shape: Every additive axis saturates by Act II — so the only rows that carry information are Sustain, Saves and Endurance, and all three are axes a partner cannot fix
bombard-riptide.damage: This pair owns the crowd fight in every act and is merely very good at the boss fight — and neither half has a dead encounter, which is the whole reason the numbers are this high

bombard-sanctum.tagline: A pair built to stop long-resting. Sanctum's Flurry of Healing and Harm converts short-rest ki into hit points, so the 120-supply rest is forced by nothing but story — and every damage resource on both sheets is either at-will or on the same short clock. The one decision that shapes both halves: Sanctum spends eleven levels on the healing engine before it touches the Zeal domain, which moves Haste and Fireball to Act III and hands the whole spell payload of Acts I–II to Bombard.
bombard-sanctum.shape: Everything except Saves and AoE is covered twice by Act III — and Saves is the axis neither character can lend the other
bombard-sanctum.damage: This pair owns priority targets from Act I and only becomes a crowd answer in Act III

bombard-fold.tagline: Fold buys the party three or four extra bodies that cost no concentration and no turn to maintain, so Bombard can spend its own concentration on the spell that ends the fight — and brand the one enemy that has to fail its save.
bombard-fold.shape: A pair that is never short of bodies, never short of hit points, and one bad Wisdom save away from losing Bombard
bombard-fold.damage: This pair owns the crowd in every act and merely survives the boss — Fold is a passenger in priority fights, deliberately
